verification_report.summary: The proof passes the strict recheck. The two-background local freezing correctly applies Dinew's bounded Lebesgue-density mixed inequality after positive quadratic corrections, and polynomial weak passage in epsilon yields the bounded trace estimate. Genuine truncation locality transfers the extended-Monge–Ampere lower bound to bounded truncations; L1 convergence of the linear currents and integrability of g^(1/n) then prove the full-current trace inequality while retaining pole-set trace mass. For a smooth normalized Gauduchon test, Stokes and the exact root formula give the positive error-measure mass identity, hence its total-variation decay uniformly in the threshold subsolution, without a root-tail condition. The separately completed root-tail/current-attainment audit (verified report SHA256 488d1ce7c37d28a181a8cd4f6f86ad3215a9a87ad5e1c6e166d74df478b79461) supplies exactly the near-maximizer weighted-measure convergence used only in the last proposition paragraph. Finally, a smooth positive dual maximizer makes the distributional difference of two threshold subsolutions solve a homogeneous smooth elliptic scalar equation, so elliptic regularity and the maximum principle prove constancy. Dinew's author v1, arXiv:0705.0974v1, Theorem 1.2 on PDF page 2 matches the cited bounded local result and its hypotheses. No unsupported finite-mass, rough-equation, singular-current-wedge, or maximizing-current-regularity claim is used.
